title: Find Min and Max
prompt: A sensor panel needs the lowest and highest reading from a batch. Write a function that returns an object with min and max values. If the input array is empty, return { min: null, max: null }.

explanation.beginner:
Example: findMinMax([4,1,9,2]) produces {"min":1,"max":9}. The result must follow this precise rule: A sensor panel needs the lowest and highest reading from a batch. Write a function that returns an object with min and max values. If the input array is empty, return { min: null, max: null }. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “handles one value”: input [[7]] produces {"min":7,"max":7}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:

If the input array is empty, return { min: null, max: null }. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the handles one value case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles one value”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
